results.fact: whether a wilderness permit is required
results.correct_value: No wilderness permit or quota for this route; only a Northwest Forest Pass for parking (access.permit 'None required' is correct).

results.fact: which side of the mountain the route climbs
results.evidence: Every account found climbs from Airplane Lake on the EAST side: one describes the east slope/east face on snow (with the ridge as an alternative), another scrambles from the lake to the ridge line on the north side of the lake, through a saddle with a class 3 rock ramp, then along the ridge to the summit. No source names a 'Southeast Slopes' line or a saddle on the southeast ridge, and the lake sits almost due east of the summit. But the route name cannot be changed here, and changing aspect/face to E alone would set them against the name, so this needs a naming decision rather than a patch.

results.correct_value: Class 3 scrambling (talus, slabs, broad ridge) with low-to-moderate exposure, not Class 2.
results.evidence: The row's grade, rock_grade, beta ('class 3 scrambling'), pro_needs, obj_haz ('class 3 ridge') and summit waypoint all say Class 3; only seasonal_hazards.exposure says Class 2. An ascent report describes a class 3 rock ramp into a saddle and a few class 3 steps on a wide ridge with nothing too difficult, supporting Class 3 with moderate exposure. Only the terrain class in the exposure line is changed.

patches.fact: how exposed the route is
patches.replace: typical of Class 3 scrambling on talus, slabs and a broad ridge

results.fact: total round-trip mileage / one-way distance to Airplane Lake and the summit
results.correct_value: Turnoff from Indian Creek Trail ~4.5 mi, Airplane Lake ~6 mi, summit ~7.5 mi one-way (~15-16 mi round trip).
results.evidence: A 2021 ascent logged trailhead to the turnoff 4.5 mi/1,200 ft, turnoff to the lake 1.5 mi/2,200 ft and lake to summit 1.5 mi/2,000 ft (7.5 mi one-way). The encyclopedia entry gives the standard route as 16 miles round trip with 5,300 ft of gain. The itinerary (6 mi to camp, 9 mi summit-and-out), the camp note (turnoff at about 4.5 miles) and dist_km (12.5 km) all agree; the waypoint cumulative distances (turnoff 3, lake 4.5, summit 6) were the outliers. Intermediate pins without a sourced distance are cleared rather than guessed; the 12-mile figure is kept as it is framed as one party's more direct line.

results.fact: Pitch count and which pitch is the crux
results.correct_value: Crux (the roofs) on pitch 2; six pitches overall, the last a short pitch from the notch past the false summit that many parties scramble.
results.evidence: The route database entry gives 6 pitches: three to a hanging slab, two more to the false summit, then a drop to a notch and one more pitch to the true summit, with pitch 2's roofs as the physical crux. A separate party's account also found pitch 2 the crux and scrambled the final gap unroped. So pitches=6 and the 5-row ROUTE BREAKDOWN (which ends by coiling the rope at the false summit) both stand; the waypoint label '(Pitch 3)' and the pro tip's alternative six-pitch numbering with the crux on P3 were the outliers.

patches.fact: Pitch count and which pitch is the crux
Pitch count and which pitch is the crux
patches.find: A commonly reported six-pitch breakdown: P1-2 climb chimney systems; P3 is the crux, a 5.6 bulge; P4 a 5.4 face with real exposure; P5 a Class 3-4 traverse across a large slab; P6 ledges and cracks to the summit — though many parties link it into just 4-5 pitches.
patches.replace: Pitch counts vary with how parties split the rope-lengths: the crux roofs come on pitch 2, three pitches reach a hanging slab, two more lead to the false summit, and a short final pitch or an exposed scramble from the notch beyond it gains the true summit.

results.fact: Car-to-car total time vs its own schedule
results.evidence: The schedule (3:30 AM start, summit ~noon, back 5-6 PM) implies 13.5-14.5 h, while totalHrs, the day hours and the notes say 11 h / 10-12 h. Reported West Ridge days span roughly 10.5 h for a fast trail-running party to about 14.3 h for a party of four (5:40 AM to 8 PM); no two sources agree on one figure, so neither the total nor the schedule was changed.
